title.zh: 卷四十 蜀書十 劉彭廖李劉魏楊傳
title.en: Volume 40: Book of Shu 10 - Biographies of Liu, Peng, Liao, Li, Liu, Wei, and Yang
title.raw: 卷四十 蜀書十 劉彭廖李劉魏楊傳 Volume 40: Book of Shu 10 - Biographies of Liu, Peng, Liao, Li, Liu, Wei, and Yang

sentences.zh: 劉封者，本羅侯寇氏之子，長沙劉氏之甥也。

translations.literal: Liu Feng was originally the son of Marquis Luo of the Kou clan and the nephew of the Liu family of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Feng was born to the Kou house of Marquis Luo and was the nephew of the Liu clan of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 先主至荊州，以未有繼嗣，養封為子。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord arrived in Jing Province, because he had yet no heir, he adopted Feng as a son.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei reached Jing Province he still had no heir, so he adopted Liu Feng as his son.

sentences.zh: 及先主入蜀，自葭萌還攻劉璋，時封年二十馀，有武藝，氣力過人，將兵俱與諸葛亮、張飛等溯流西上，所在戰克。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord entered Shu and turned back from Jiameng to attack Liu Zhang, at that time Feng was over twenty, had martial skill, and strength surpassing others; he led troops together with Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, and others up the river westward, winning victory wherever they fought.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei marched into Shu from Jiameng against Liu Zhang, Liu Feng was already in his twenties—strong, skilled in arms, and bold enough to lead men beside Zhuge Liang and Zhang Fei upriver into the west, victorious at every turn.

sentences.zh: 益州既定，以封為副軍中郎將。

translations.literal: After Yi Province was settled, Feng was appointed General of the Household, Deputy to the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yi Province was secured, Liu Feng became a general of the household serving as deputy to the army.

sentences.zh: 初，劉璋遣扶風孟達副法正，各將兵二千人，使迎先主，先主因令達並領其眾，留屯江陵。

translations.literal: At first Liu Zhang sent Fufeng’s Meng Da as deputy to Fa Zheng; each led two thousand troops to welcome the Former Lord; the Former Lord then ordered Da also to command their hosts and left them garrisoned at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: At first Liu Zhang sent Meng Da of Fufeng to assist Fa Zheng; each brought two thousand men to greet Liu Bei, who then put Meng Da in charge of both contingents and left them holding Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 蜀平後，以達為宜都太守。

translations.literal: After Shu was pacified, Da was made Governor of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest he named Meng Da governor of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 建安二十四年，命達從秭歸北攻房陵，房陵太守蒯祺為達兵所害。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian’an he ordered Da from Zigui to attack Fangling to the north; Fangling Governor Kuai Qi was killed by Da’s troops.
translations.idiomatic: In 219 Meng Da was ordered north from Zigui against Fangling; Governor Kuai Qi fell to his attack.

sentences.zh: 達將進攻上庸，先主陰恐達難獨任，乃遣封自漢中乘沔水下統達軍，與達會上庸。

translations.literal: As Da was about to advance on Shangyong, the Former Lord secretly feared Da could not shoulder the task alone; he therefore sent Feng from Hanzhong down the Mian River to take command of Da’s army and join Da at Shangyong.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Meng Da could not take Shangyong alone, Liu Bei sent Liu Feng from Hanzhong down the Han River to assume command of his troops and link up at Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 上庸太守申耽舉眾降，遣妻子及宗族詣成都。

translations.literal: Shangyong Governor Shen Dan surrendered with his whole force, sending wife, children, and clan members to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Dan of Shangyong capitulated with his entire command and sent his family and kin to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 先主加耽征北將軍，領上庸太守員鄉侯如故，以耽弟儀為建信將軍、西城太守，遷封為副軍將軍。

translations.literal: The Former Lord added Dan as General Who Conquers the North, continuing as before as Governor of Shangyong and Marquis of Yuan Village; he made Dan’s younger brother Yi General Who Establishes Trust and Governor of Xicheng, and promoted Feng to General of the Army, Deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei named Shen Dan general who conquers the north and left him marquis of Yuan Village as governor of Shangyong; Shen Yi became general who establishes trust and governor of Xicheng; Liu Feng rose to deputy army commander.

sentences.zh: 自關羽圍樊城、襄陽，連呼封、達，令發兵自助。

translations.literal: From when Guan Yu besieged Fancheng and Xiangyang, he repeatedly summoned Feng and Da, ordering them to raise troops to assist himself.
translations.idiomatic: While Guan Yu besieged Fancheng and Xiangyang he repeatedly called on Liu Feng and Meng Da to send reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 封、達辭以山郡初附，未可動搖，不承羽命。

translations.literal: Feng and Da declined on the grounds that the mountain commanderies had newly submitted and could not be disturbed; they did not obey Yu’s order.
translations.idiomatic: They refused, pleading that the hill country had only just submitted and could not be risked, and ignored Guan Yu’s command.

sentences.zh: 會羽覆敗，先主恨之。

translations.literal: It happened that Yu was utterly defeated; the Former Lord resented them.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Yu was destroyed, Liu Bei blamed them both.

sentences.zh: 又封與達忿爭不和，封尋奪達鼓吹。

translations.literal: Moreover Feng quarrelled with Da and they did not get along; Feng shortly seized Da’s ceremonial band.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Feng also feuded with Meng Da and soon stripped him of his ceremonial musicians.

sentences.zh: 達既懼罪，又忿恚封，遂表辭先主，率所領降魏。

translations.literal: Da both feared punishment and resented Feng; he then memorialized his farewell to the Former Lord and led his command to surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Da, fearing execution and furious at Liu Feng, submitted a resignation to Liu Bei and defected to Wei with his troops.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》載達辭先主表曰：「伏惟殿下將建伊、呂之業，追桓、文之功，大事草創，假勢吳、楚，是以有為之士深睹歸趣。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Summary carries Da’s memorial of farewell to the Former Lord, saying, “I humbly consider that Your Highness will establish the enterprises of Yi Yin and Lü Shang and pursue the achievements of Huan and Wen; the great task is newly begun; borrowing strength from Wu and Chu—therefore men of purpose deeply see where allegiance lies.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei Summary preserves Meng Da’s memorial: “Your Highness pursues the legacies of Yi Yin and Lü Wang and the hegemony of Huan and Wen; the enterprise is still young and leans on Wu and Chu—men of ambition know where to turn.”

sentences.zh: 臣委質已來，愆戾山積，臣猶自知，況於君乎！

translations.literal: Since I pledged myself, faults have piled like mountains—I know this myself; how much more my lord!”
translations.idiomatic: Since I pledged my service, my offenses have stacked high—I know it, and how much more must you!”

sentences.zh: 今王朝以興，英俊鱗集，臣內無輔佐之器，外無將領之才，列次功臣，誠自愧也。

translations.literal: Now the royal court rises; heroes gather like scales; I lack inner capacity to assist and outer talent to command—ranked among meritorious ministers, I am truly ashamed.”
translations.idiomatic: Now the court flourishes and talent crowds in; I have neither administrative gifts nor martial gifts among your servants—I blush to stand even on the roll of honour.”

sentences.zh: 臣聞范蠡識微，浮於五湖；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Fan Li sensed the subtlety and floated on the Five Lakes;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li read the signs and sailed the Five Lakes;

sentences.zh: 咎犯謝罪，逡巡於河上。

translations.literal: Jiu Fan apologized for crime and hesitated on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu Fan waited his lord’s pardon by the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 夫際會之間，請命乞身。

translations.literal: At meetings of circumstance they begged their lives and bodies.
translations.idiomatic: At such turning points wise men beg leave to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 欲絜去就之分也。

translations.literal: They wished to clarify the boundary between going and staying.
translations.idiomatic: They wished to keep honour whole when staying or leaving.

sentences.zh: 況臣卑鄙，無元功巨勳，自系於時，竊慕前賢，早思遠恥。

translations.literal: Moreover your servant is base and mean, without founding merit or great deed; tied by circumstance, I secretly admire former worthies and long ago ponder distant shame.
translations.idiomatic: I am mean and small, with no great merit to my name; bound by events, I emulate the ancients and flee humiliation early.

sentences.zh: 昔申生至孝見疑於親，子胥至忠見誅於君，蒙恬拓境而被大刑，樂毅破齊而遭讒佞，臣每讀其書，未嘗不慷慨流涕，而親當其事，益以傷絕。

translations.literal: Of old Shensheng was supremely filial yet suspected by kin; Wu Zixu supremely loyal yet executed by his lord; Meng Tian expanded the borders yet suffered great punishment; Yue Yi broke Qi yet met slander—each time I read their tales I never fail to weep with passion; now I face the matter myself and am all the more broken-hearted.
translations.idiomatic: Shensheng’s filial piety earned suspicion; Wu Zixu’s loyalty brought death; Meng Tian died after conquering new lands; Yue Yi fell to calumny after crushing Qi—I have always wept over such stories; to live them myself is worse still.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 荊州覆敗，大臣失節，百無一還。

translations.literal: Jing Province was overturned and defeated; great ministers lost their integrity—of a hundred not one returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jing fell; not one defector in a hundred kept his honour.

sentences.zh: 惟臣尋事，自致房陵、上庸，而復乞身，自放於外。

translations.literal: Only your servant pursued affairs and brought himself to Fangling and Shangyong, then again begged his person and released himself abroad.
translations.idiomatic: I alone carved out Fangling and Shangyong, then asked to step aside and live at the margin.

sentences.zh: 伏想殿下聖恩感悟，愍臣之心，悼臣之舉。

translations.literal: I humbly imagine Your Highness’s sacred grace will awaken to pity your servant’s heart and mourn your servant’s act.
translations.idiomatic: I trust Your Highness’s kindness will pity my heart and regret my choice.

sentences.zh: 臣誠小人，不能始終，知而為之，敢謂非罪！

translations.literal: Your servant is truly a petty man, unable to finish what he began—knowing yet doing it, how dare I call it no crime!”
translations.idiomatic: I am a small man who could not see things through; I knew the risk and took it—how can I claim innocence!”

sentences.zh: 臣每間交絕無惡聲，去臣無怨辭，臣過奉教於君子，原君王勉之也。」〉

translations.literal: Whenever ties break, let there be no angry words; when I depart, let there be no resentful speech—I have received instruction from gentlemen; I beg my lord to understand.”〉
translations.idiomatic: Partings need no bitter words, banishment no grudge—I have heard gentlemen teach thus; I pray you take it to heart.”〉

sentences.zh: 魏文帝善達之姿才容觀，以為散騎常侍、建武將軍，封平陽亭侯。

translations.literal: Wei Wendi approved Da’s bearing, talent, and appearance; he made him Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Establishes Martial Might, and enfeoffed him Marquis of Pingyang village.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi admired Meng Da’s presence and ability, named him palace attendant and general who establishes martial might, and made him village marquis of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 合房陵、上庸、西城三郡〔為新城郡，以〕達領新城太守。

translations.literal: He merged the three commanderies of Fangling, Shangyong, and Xicheng [into New City commandery and] made Da concurrent Governor of New City.
translations.idiomatic: He merged Fangling, Shangyong, and Xicheng into New City commandery and put Meng Da in charge.

sentences.zh: 遣征南將軍夏侯尚、右將軍徐晃與達共襲封。

translations.literal: He sent General Who Conquers the South Xiahou Shang and General of the Right Xu Huang together with Da to strike Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Xiahou Shang and Xu Huang with Meng Da against Liu Feng.

sentences.zh: 達與封書曰：

translations.literal: Da wrote a letter to Feng, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Meng Da wrote to Liu Feng:

sentences.zh: 古人有言：『疏不間親，新不加舊。

translations.literal: The ancients said: “The distant do not come between the close; the new does not rank above the old.”
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: “Outsiders cannot divide kin; newcomers cannot supplant old retainers.”

sentences.zh: 』此謂上明下直，讒慝不行也。

translations.literal: ” This means when the ruler is enlightened and subordinates upright, slander and evil cannot operate.
translations.idiomatic: That holds when the sovereign is clear-sighted and ministers straightforward—slander then finds no foothold.

sentences.zh: 若乃權君譎主，賢父慈親，猶有忠臣蹈功以罹禍，孝子抱仁以陷難，種、商、白起、孝己、伯奇，皆其類也。

translations.literal: Yet twisted rulers and deceitful lords, worthy fathers and loving parents, still had loyal ministers who followed merit and met disaster, filial sons who embraced benevolence and fell into hardship—Wen Zhong, Bai Qi, filial Ji, Boyi—their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Even under capricious fathers and sage parents, loyal servants still died for their deeds and filial sons for their love—Wen Zhong, Lord Shang, Bai Qi, Xiao Ji, and Boyi all belong to that tale.

sentences.zh: 其所以然，非骨肉好離，親親樂患也。

translations.literal: The reason is not that flesh and blood love separation or that kinfolk delight in calamity.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that kin love estrangement or welcome ruin.

sentences.zh: 或有恩移愛易，亦有讒間其間，雖忠臣不能移之於君，孝子不能變之於父者也。

translations.literal: Sometimes favour shifts and love changes; sometimes slander drives in between—though a loyal minister cannot move his lord, a filial son cannot alter his father.
translations.idiomatic: Favour shifts, love turns, and whisperers slip between—even loyal ministers cannot sway every ruler, nor filial sons every father.

sentences.zh: 勢利所加，改親為讎，況非親親乎！

translations.literal: When power and profit bear down, kin become foes—how much more when there is no blood tie!
translations.idiomatic: Interest turns kin into enemies—what of mere adoption?

sentences.zh: 故申生、衛伋、禦寇、楚建禀受形之氣，當嗣立之正，而猶如此。

translations.literal: Therefore Shensheng, Wei Ji, Yu Kou, and Chu Jian received their bodily qi with rightful claim to succession, yet still came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Shensheng, Ji of Wei, Yu Kou, and Jian of Chu were lawful heirs—yet each met doom.

sentences.zh: 今足下與漢中王，道路之人耳，親非骨血而據勢權，義非君臣而處上位，徵則有偏任之威，居則有副軍之號，遠近所聞也。

translations.literal: Now you and the King of Hanzhong are but fellow travellers on the road—not bone and blood yet holding power and rank; not lord and minister by duty yet occupying high station; when campaigning you wield favoritism’s weight, at rest you bear the deputy army’s title—far and near have heard it.
translations.idiomatic: You and the King of Hanzhong are strangers by blood yet you wield real power; you are no true minister yet stand high; in the field you hold disproportionate authority, at court the title of deputy commander—the whole realm knows it.

sentences.zh: 自立阿斗為太子已來，有識之人相為寒心。

translations.literal: From the day Adou was established heir, every thoughtful man has shivered.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Shan was named heir, thinking men have trembled.

sentences.zh: 如使申生從子輿之言，必為太伯；

translations.literal: Had Shensheng followed Ziyu’s words, he would surely have become Taibo;
translations.idiomatic: Had Shensheng heeded his tutor he might have become another Taibo;

sentences.zh: 衛伋聽其弟之謀，無彰父之譏也。

translations.literal: had Wei Ji listened to his younger brother’s plan, there would have been no reproach that shamed the father.
translations.idiomatic: had Ji of Wei trusted his brother’s counsel, his father would not have been shamed.

sentences.zh: 且小白出奔，入而為霸；

translations.literal: Moreover Little Bai fled out and entered to become hegemon;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan fled Qi yet returned to lead the alliance;

sentences.zh: 重耳踰垣，卒以克復。

translations.literal: Chong’er climbed the wall and in the end recovered all.
translations.idiomatic: Chong’er scaled the wall and won his state back.

sentences.zh: 自古有之，非獨今也。

translations.literal: Since antiquity it has been thus—not only today.
translations.idiomatic: Such turns are old news, not news from our age alone.

sentences.zh: 夫智貴免禍，明尚夙達，僕揆漢中王慮定於內，疑生於外矣；

translations.literal: Wisdom prizes escaping calamity; insight esteems foresight early—I gauge that the King of Hanzhong has settled his mind within and suspicion arises without;
translations.idiomatic: The wise flee disaster and foresee trouble early—I believe the King of Hanzhong has made his decision within while doubt gathers without;

sentences.zh: 慮定則心固，疑生則心懼，亂禍之興作，未曾不由廢立之間也。

translations.literal: when the mind is settled the heart is firm; when suspicion arises the heart fears—turmoil and disaster never fail to spring from the interval of deposing and establishing.
translations.idiomatic: resolve breeds confidence, suspicion breeds fear—every throne struggle proves it.

sentences.zh: 私怨人情，不能不見，恐左右必有以間於漢中王矣。

translations.literal: Private resentment is human feeling—it cannot help but show; I fear those about him surely speak against you to the King of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Men nurse private grudges—I fear someone whispers against you in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 然則疑成怨聞，其發若踐機耳。

translations.literal: Then suspicion forms and resentment is heard—its release is like treading a trigger.
translations.idiomatic: Once suspicion hardens, the trap springs like a sprung crossbow.

sentences.zh: 今足下在遠，尚可假息一時；

translations.literal: Now you are far away—you may still catch your breath for a while;
translations.idiomatic: Distance still buys you a little time;

sentences.zh: 若大軍遂進，足下失據而還，竊相為危之。

translations.literal: but if the great army advances and you lose footing and return, I privately think danger for you.
translations.idiomatic: when our hosts close in and you retreat stripped of position, I tremble for you.

sentences.zh: 昔微子去殷，智果別族，違難背禍，猶皆如斯。

translations.literal: Of old Weizi left Yin; Zhiguo split his clan—fleeing hardship and turning from disaster, all were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Weizi fled Yin; Zhiguo split his lineage—wise men dodge ruin this way.

sentences.zh: 〈國語曰：智宣子將以瑤為後，智果曰：「不如霄也。

translations.literal: 〈The Discourses of the States says: Lord Xuan of Zhi was about to make Yao his heir; Zhiguo said, “Better Xia.”
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Discourses of the States tells how Lord Xuan of Zhi meant to choose Yao until Zhiguo urged Xia instead.”

sentences.zh: 」宣子曰：「霄也佷。

translations.literal: ” Lord Xuan said, “Xia is brutal.”
translations.idiomatic: “Xia is brutal,” said Lord Xuan.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「霄也佷在面，瑤之賢於人者五，其不逮者一也。

translations.literal: ” He replied, “Xia’s brutality shows on his face; Yao surpasses men in five ways—what he lacks is one.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguo answered: “Xia’s cruelty shows on his skin; Yao excels in five talents yet lacks humaneness.”

sentences.zh: 美須長大則賢，射禦足力則賢，技藝畢給則賢，巧文辯惠則賢，強毅果敢則賢，如是而甚不仁；

translations.literal: Fine beard and tall stature counts as worthy; archery and charioteering and foot strength counts as worthy; skills fully supplied counts as worthy; clever writing and eloquent wit counts as worthy; strength and resolve and daring counts as worthy—thus yet deeply inhumane;
translations.idiomatic: Long beard and tall frame, shooting and riding, every craft, fluent speech, iron nerve—all marks of talent—yet wholly ruthless;

sentences.zh: 以五者賢陵人，而不仁行之，其誰能待之！

translations.literal: with five kinds of excellence he overrides others and acts without benevolence—who can endure him!
translations.idiomatic: five virtues deployed without mercy will destroy everyone around him!”

sentences.zh: 若果立瑤也。

translations.literal: If indeed Yao is established.
translations.idiomatic: If you raise Yao,”

sentences.zh: 智宗必滅。

translations.literal: The Zhi lineage will surely perish.
translations.idiomatic: the house of Zhi will fall.”

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: ” He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Xuan refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 智果別族於太史氏為輔氏。

translations.literal: Zhiguo split his clan from the Grand Scribe’s house and became the Fu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguo registered his line separately as the Fu clan.

sentences.zh: 及智氏亡，惟輔果在焉。〉

translations.literal: When the Zhi clan perished, only Fuguo survived.〉
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi fell, only Fuguo remained.〉

sentences.zh: 今足下棄父母而為人後，非禮也；

translations.literal: Now you abandon parents to become another’s heir—it is not ritual;
translations.idiomatic: You turned your back on your birth parents to be adopted—against propriety;

sentences.zh: 知禍將至而留之，非智也；

translations.literal: knowing disaster will come yet staying—not wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: to see disaster coming yet linger—not wisdom;

sentences.zh: 見正不從而疑之，非義也。

translations.literal: seeing the right and not following yet doubting—not righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: to hear sound counsel and doubt it—not honour.

sentences.zh: 自號為丈夫，為此三者，何所貴乎？

translations.literal: Calling yourself a man while doing these three—what is there to honour?
translations.idiomatic: You style yourself a hero yet break three cardinal virtues—what remains to respect?

sentences.zh: 以足下之才，棄身來東，繼嗣羅侯，不為背親也；

translations.literal: With your talent, leave yourself and come east, inherit Marquis Luo—it is not betraying kin;
translations.idiomatic: Come east with your gifts and resume the Luo marquisate—you would not betray your blood;

sentences.zh: 北面事君，以正綱紀，不為棄舊也；

translations.literal: face north and serve a lord, rectifying the norms—not abandoning the old;
translations.idiomatic: serve the Son of Heaven and restore order—you would not cast off the past;

sentences.zh: 怒不致亂，以免危亡，不為徒行也。

translations.literal: anger not reaching chaos, thereby escaping peril—not empty motion.
translations.idiomatic: withdraw without sparking revolt and save your skin—that is no idle gesture.

sentences.zh: 加陛下新受禪命，虛心側席，以德懷遠，若足下翻然內向，非但與僕為倫，受三百戶封，繼統羅國而已，當更剖符大邦，為始封之君。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty has newly received the abdication mandate, empties his heart and leaves the mat aside, embracing the distant with virtue—if you turn about toward the inner court, you will not only match your servant, receive a three-hundred-household fief, and continue the Luo state—you will further split tallies in a great region and be its first enfeoffed lord.
translations.idiomatic: Our new emperor hungers for loyal talent: return and you will rank beside me, keep your three-hundred-household fief and the Luo succession, and likely gain a great province with bronze tallies.

sentences.zh: 陛下大軍，金鼓以震，當轉都宛、鄧；

translations.literal: Your Majesty’s great army, drums and gongs shaking, will shift the capital toward Wan and Deng;
translations.idiomatic: The imperial host will soon roll toward Wan and Deng;

sentences.zh: 若二敵不平，軍無還期。

translations.literal: if the two foes are not pacified, the army has no date of return.
translations.idiomatic: until Shu and Wu yield, there will be no going home.

sentences.zh: 足下宜因此時早定良計。

translations.literal: You ought at this time early settle a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: Choose your course before it is chosen for you.

sentences.zh: 易有『利見大人』，詩有『自求多福』，行矣。

translations.literal: The Changes has ‘It furthers one to see the great man’; the Odes has ‘Seek much blessing for yourself’—go.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou yi promises blessing for those who approach greatness; the Odes urge men to win their own fortune—act.

sentences.zh: 今足下勉之，無使狐突閉門不出。

translations.literal: Now strive, sir—do not make Hutu shut his gate and never come out.
translations.idiomatic: Move now—do not die like Hutu, who never ventured forth again.

sentences.zh: 封不從達言。

translations.literal: Feng did not follow Da’s words.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Feng ignored him.

sentences.zh: 申儀叛封，封破走還成都。

translations.literal: Shen Yi rebelled against Feng; Feng was defeated and fled back to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yi turned on Liu Feng, who broke and ran to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 申耽降魏，魏假耽懷集將軍，徙居南陽，儀魏興太守，封

translations.literal: Shen Dan surrendered to Wei; Wei made Dan provisional General Who Cherishes and Gathers, moved him to reside in Nanyang; Yi was Wei Governor of Weixing, enfeoffed
translations.idiomatic: Shen Dan went over to Wei as general who cherishes and gathers and retired to Nanyang; Shen Yi became Wei’s governor of Weixing and was enfeoffed

sentences.zh: （真鄉侯）

translations.literal: (Marquis of Zhen Village)
translations.idiomatic: 〈variant: Marquis of Zhen Village〉

sentences.zh: 〔員鄉侯〕，屯洵口。

translations.literal: [Marquis of Yuan Village], garrisoned at Xunkou.
translations.idiomatic: marquis of Yuan Village, with troops at Xunkou.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：申儀兄名耽，字義舉。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Summary states: Shen Yi’s elder brother was named Dan, courtesy name Yiju.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei Summary identifies Shen Dan, styled Yiju, as Shen Yi’s elder brother.

sentences.zh: 初在西平、上庸間聚眾數千家，後與張魯通，又遣使詣曹公，曹公加其號為將軍，因使領上庸都尉。

translations.literal: At first between Xiping and Shangyong he gathered several thousand households; later he communicated with Zhang Lu and also sent envoys to Duke Cao; Duke Cao added his title as general and thereby made him commandant of Shangyong.
translations.idiomatic: He first raised thousands of families between Xiping and Shangyong, then dealt with Zhang Lu and Cao Cao, who named him general and commandant of Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 至建安末，為蜀所攻，以其郡西屬。

translations.literal: By the end of Jian’an he was attacked by Shu and attached his commandery to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jian’an era Liu Bei pressed him and he submitted his territory westward.

sentences.zh: 黃初中，儀復來還，詔即以兄故號加儀，因拜魏興太守，封列侯。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu era Yi came back; an edict used his brother’s former title for Yi, therefore appointed him Governor of Weixing and enfeoffed him as a full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangchu he returned and inherited his brother’s rank as governor of Weixing and full marquis.

sentences.zh: 太和中，儀與孟達不和，數上言達有貳心於蜀，及達反，儀絕蜀道，使救不到。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era Yi did not get along with Meng Da and repeatedly memorialized that Da had divided loyalty toward Shu; when Da rebelled, Yi cut Shu’s roads so relief could not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe he feuded with Meng Da, accused him of dealing with Shu, and blocked Shu’s roads when Meng Da rose.

sentences.zh: 達死後，儀詣宛見司馬宣王，宣王勸使來朝。

translations.literal: After Da died, Yi went to Wan to see Sima Yi; Sima Yi urged him to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: After Meng Da fell Shen Yi saw Sima Yi at Wan and was urged to visit Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 儀至京師，詔轉拜儀樓船將軍，在禮請中。〉

translations.literal: When Yi reached the capital, an edict transferred him to General of the Tower Ships, among those invited by ritual.〉
translations.idiomatic: At the capital he became general of the tower ships, honoured among invited ministers.〉

sentences.zh: 封既至，先主責封之侵陵達，又不救羽。

translations.literal: When Feng arrived, the Former Lord blamed Feng for bullying Da and for not rescuing Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei rebuked Liu Feng for humiliating Meng Da and refusing Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮慮封剛猛，易世之後終難制御，勸先主因此除之。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang worried Feng was fierce and stubborn—after the succession changed he would finally be hard to control—and urged the Former Lord therefore to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang feared his fierce temper would menace the next reign and urged Liu Bei to remove him.

sentences.zh: 於是賜封死，使自裁。

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted Feng death, ordering him to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Feng was ordered to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 封歎曰：「恨不用孟子度之言！

translations.literal: Feng sighed, saying, “I regret not using Meng Zidu’s words!”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Feng cried, “If only I had listened to Meng Da!”

sentences.zh: 」先主為之流涕。

translations.literal: ” The Former Lord wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei wept for him.

sentences.zh: 達本字子敬，避先主叔父敬，改之。

translations.literal: Da’s original courtesy name was Zijing; to avoid the Former Lord’s uncle Jing, it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Da had first styled himself Zijing but changed it to avoid Liu Bei’s uncle’s name.

sentences.zh: 〈封子林為牙門將，咸熙元年內移河東。

translations.literal: 〈Feng’s son Lin was Colonel of the Ya Gate; in the first year of Xianxi he was moved inward to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Liu Feng’s son Liu Lin became a gate colonel and moved family to Hedong in 264.

sentences.zh: 達子興為議督軍，是歲徙還扶風。〉

translations.literal: Da’s son Xing was advisory supervisor of the army; that year he was moved back to Fufeng.〉
translations.idiomatic: Meng Da’s son Meng Xing served as staff supervisor and returned the clan to Fufeng that year.〉

sentences.zh: 彭羕字永年，廣漢人。

translations.literal: Peng Yang, courtesy name Yongnian, was a man of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yang, styled Yongnian, came from Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，容貌甚偉。

translations.literal: He was eight chi in height and his bearing was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall and cut an imposing figure.

sentences.zh: 姿性驕傲，多所輕忽，惟敬同郡秦子敕，薦之於太守許靖曰：

translations.literal: In temperament he was arrogant and slighted many; he only respected Qin Zici of the same commandery, and recommended him to Governor Xu Jing, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Proud and dismissive of most men, he respected only Qin Zici of his county and wrote to Governor Xu Jing:

sentences.zh: 昔高宗夢傅說，周文求呂尚，爰及漢祖，納食其於布衣，此乃帝王之所以倡業垂統，緝熙厥功也。

translations.literal: Of old Gaozong dreamed of Fu Yue; King Wen of Zhou sought Lü Shang; reaching to the Han ancestor, he took Lis Yi from plain cloth—this is how emperors and kings begin enterprise and hand down succession, extending and brightening their merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient founders summoned ministers from dreams, rivers, and the marketplace—such is how dynasties begin and merit shines on.

sentences.zh: 今明府稽古皇極，允執神靈，體公劉之德，行勿翦之惠，清廟之作於是乎始，褒貶之義於是乎興，然而六翮未之備也。

translations.literal: Now your enlightened office examines antiquity at the royal pivot, sincerely holds the spirits, embodies Duke Liu’s virtue, practises kindness undimmed—the Pure Temple’s work begins here, praise and blame arise here—yet the six wing-pinions are not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: You revive classical rule and humane government fit for the ancestral shrine—yet your wings are not fully grown.

sentences.zh: 伏見處士綿竹秦宓，膺山甫之德，履雋生之直，枕石漱流，吟詠缊袍，偃息於仁義之途，恬惔於浩然之域，高概節行，守真不虧，雖古人潛遁，蔑以加旃。

translations.literal: I humbly observe the recluse Qin Mi of Mianzhu, bearing the virtue of Shanfu, treading the uprightness of Junsheng—pillowing on stone, rinsing mouth in streams, chanting in patched robes, resting on the road of benevolence and righteousness, tranquil in the vast realm—lofty principle and conduct, guarding truth without flaw—even ancient men who hid away could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Mi of Mianzhu lives the life of a sage recluse—streams for drink, patched robes, content within humanity’s way—no ancient hermit could outshine him.

sentences.zh: 若明府能招致此人，必有忠讜落落之譽，豐功厚利，建跡立勳，然後紀功於王府，飛聲於來世，不亦美哉！」

translations.literal: If your enlightened office can win this man, there will surely be praise for blunt loyalty standing tall; abundant deeds and lasting profit; traces raised and merit established—then merit recorded at the royal court and fame sent to later ages—is it not fine!”
translations.idiomatic: Bring him in and you gain frank counsel and deeds worthy of the histories—is that not splendid!”

sentences.zh: 羕仕州，不過書佐，後又為眾人所謗毀於州牧劉璋，璋髡鉗羕為徒隸。

translations.literal: Yang served the province as no more than a clerk; later the multitude also slandered him before Governor Liu Zhang; Zhang shaved Yang and fitted him with the cangue as convict labour.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yang held only a clerkship in Yi; enemies maligned him to Liu Zhang, who shaved his head, shackled him, and bound him to labour gangs.

sentences.zh: 會先主入蜀，溯流北行。

translations.literal: It happened that the Former Lord entered Shu, travelling north against the current.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei marched into Shu upriver,

sentences.zh: 羕欲納說先主，乃往見龐統。

translations.literal: Yang wished to present counsel to the Former Lord; he therefore went to see Pang Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yang sought an introduction and called on Pang Tong.

sentences.zh: 統與羕非故人，又適有賓客，羕徑上統床臥，謂統曰：「須客罷當與卿善談。

translations.literal: Tong and Yang were not old friends; moreover there happened to be guests; Yang went straight onto Tong’s couch and lay down, saying to Tong, “When the guests leave I shall have a proper talk with you.”
translations.idiomatic: Strangers though they were, and Pang Tong had guests, Peng Yang stretched out on his couch: “When they go, we talk.”

sentences.zh: 」統客既罷，往就羕坐，羕又先責統食，然後共語，因留信宿，至於經日。

translations.literal: ” When Tong’s guests had finished, he went to Yang’s seat; Yang again first demanded food of Tong, then they spoke together; therefore he stayed two nights, lasting through a full day.
translations.idiomatic: When the hall emptied, Pang Tong joined him; Peng Yang insisted on dinner first—they talked two days straight.

sentences.zh: 統大善之，而法正宿自知羕，遂並致之先主。

translations.literal: Tong greatly approved him; moreover Fa Zheng had long known Yang himself; therefore together they presented him to the Former Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Tong was delighted; Fa Zheng already knew Peng Yang—they presented him together to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 先主亦以為奇，數令羕宣傳軍事，指授諸將，奉使稱意，識遇日加。

translations.literal: The Former Lord also thought him extraordinary; repeatedly ordered Yang to proclaim military affairs and instruct the generals; missions matched intent; recognition and favour daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei prized him, sent him repeatedly to brief generals; every mission succeeded and his standing rose.

sentences.zh: 成都既定，先主領益州牧，拔羕為治中從事。

translations.literal: After Chengdu was settled, the Former Lord held governorship of Yi Province and promoted Yang to Clerk of the Bureau of Administration.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengdu fell, Liu Bei made him administrative clerk of Yi province.

sentences.zh: 羕起徒步，一朝處州人之上，形色囂然，自矜得遇滋甚。

translations.literal: Yang rose from walking alone; in one morning he stood above the province’s men—his manner loudly arrogant; he prided himself on receiving favour ever more greatly.
translations.idiomatic: From foot soldier to head of the provincial roll overnight, he swaggered and gloated over imperial favour.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮雖外接待羕，而內不能善。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang although outwardly received Yang, inwardly could not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang was polite in public but could not abide him within.

sentences.zh: 屢密言先主，羕心大誌廣，難可保安。

translations.literal: He repeatedly spoke secretly to the Former Lord that Yang’s heart was greatly ambitious and broad—hard to keep secure.
translations.idiomatic: He warned Liu Bei again and again that Peng Yang’s vaulting ambition made him unsafe.

sentences.zh: 先主既敬信亮，加察羕行事，意以稍疏，左遷羕為江陽太守。

translations.literal: The Former Lord since he revered and trusted Liang, moreover observed Yang’s conduct—intent gradually grew distant; demoted Yang to Governor of Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting Zhuge Liang, Liu Bei cooled toward Peng Yang and named him governor of Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 羕聞當遠出，私情不悅，往詣馬超。

translations.literal: When Yang heard he would go far away, private feeling was unhappy; he went to visit Ma Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter at reassignment, he went to Ma Chao.

sentences.zh: 超問羕曰：「卿才具秀拔，主公相待至重，謂卿當與孔明、孝直諸人齊足並驅，寧當外授小郡，失人本望乎？

translations.literal: Chao asked Yang, saying, “Your talents stand out; the lord treats you with utmost weight—he thought you should pace alongside Kongming, Xiaozhi, and the rest—how could you be sent out to a small commandery, failing men’s original hope?”
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao asked how a man ranked with Zhuge Liang and Fa Zheng could be banished to a border town.

sentences.zh: 」羕曰：「老革荒悖，可複道邪！」

translations.literal: ” Yang said, “The old hide is wild and perverse—can it be spoken of again!”
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yang answered, “That worn-out hide is senile—say no more!”

sentences.zh: 〈揚雄《方言》曰：悈、鰓、乾、都、耇、革，老也。

translations.literal: 〈Yang Xiong’s Regional Words says: jie, sai, gan, du, gou, and ge mean “old.”
translations.idiomatic: 〈Yang Xiong’s Fangyan lists ge among words for old age.

sentences.zh: 郭璞注曰：皆老者皮毛枯瘁之形也。

translations.literal: Guo Pu’s commentary says: all describe the withered skin and hair of old age.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu glosses them as images of decrepitude.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以為皮去毛曰革。

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi thinks: hide stripped of fur is called ge.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that de-haired hide is called ge.

sentences.zh: 古者以革為兵，故語稱兵革，革猶兵也。

translations.literal: In antiquity ge was used for arms; therefore speech calls arms bing ge—ge is still “soldier.”
translations.idiomatic: Ancient parlance tied weapons to leather armour—here ge refers to soldiers.

sentences.zh: 羕罵備為老革，猶言老兵也。〉

translations.literal: Yang reviled Bei as old ge—it is still speaking of an old soldier.〉
translations.idiomatic: Calling Liu Bei “old leather” meant “old campaigner.”〉

sentences.zh: 又謂超曰：「卿為其外，我為其內，天下不足定也。

translations.literal: He further said to Chao, “You hold the outer line; I hold the inner—the Under Heaven is not enough to settle.”
translations.idiomatic: He added: “You outside and I inside—we could seize the realm.”

sentences.zh: 」超羈旅歸國，常懷危懼，聞羕言大驚，默然不答。

translations.literal: ” Chao was a stranded traveller come home to the state, always harbouring peril and fear; hearing Yang’s words he was greatly alarmed and silently did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao, already fearful as a former foe now serving Shu, listened in horror and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 羕退，具表羕辭，於是收羕付有司。

translations.literal: When Yang withdrew, he fully memorialized Yang’s words; therefore Yang was seized and handed to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Yang left, Ma Chao reported every word; Peng Yang was arrested.

sentences.zh: 羕於獄中與諸葛亮書曰：

translations.literal: Yang in prison wrote to Zhuge Liang, saying:
translations.idiomatic: From prison Peng Yang wrote to Zhuge Liang:

sentences.zh: 僕昔有事於諸侯，以為曹操暴虐，孫權無道，振威闇弱，其惟主公有霸王之器，可與興業致治，故乃翻然有輕舉之志。

translations.literal: Your servant once served among the lords; I thought Cao Cao cruel and violent, Sun Quan without the Way, Liu Zhang the Awesome dim and weak—only the lord possessed the capacity of a hegemon, could raise enterprise and bring good order; therefore I suddenly had the resolve of a light rising.
translations.idiomatic: I once judged Cao Cao cruel, Sun Quan lawless, and Liu Zhang feeble—only Liu Bei had hegemonic gifts; I rose to follow him.

sentences.zh: 會公來西，僕因法孝直自衒鬻，龐統斟酌其間，遂得詣公於葭萌，指掌而譚，論治世之務，講霸王之義，建取益州之策，公亦宿慮明定，即相然贊，遂舉事焉。

translations.literal: When you, sir, came west, your servant through Fa Xiaozhi peddled himself; Pang Tong mediated between; thus I reached you at Jiameng—finger-counting talk on ordering the age’s tasks, lecturing hegemon-kingship’s meaning, proposing the plan to take Yi Province; you too had long pondered and settled clearly—at once mutually approved; thus the affair was raised.
translations.idiomatic: Through Fa Zheng and Pang Tong I met you at Jiameng; we mapped Yi’s conquest and you agreed—we struck.

sentences.zh: 僕於故州不免凡庸，憂於罪罔，得遭風雲激矢之中，求君得君，志行名顯，從布衣之中擢為國士，盜竊茂才。

translations.literal: Your servant in his old province could not escape common mediocrity; worried by guilt’s net; encountered amid wind-clouds and flying arrows—sought a lord and gained a lord; ambition fulfilled and name displayed; raised from plain cloth to state gentleman—stolen Flourishing Talent nomination.
translations.idiomatic: I was a mediocrity in Yi until fate lifted me from obscurity to serve you—I even stole a “flourishing talent” nomination.

sentences.zh: 分子之厚，誰復過此。

translations.literal: The kindness of dividing sons—who again surpasses this?
translations.idiomatic: Your kindness surpasses that between father and son.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以為「分子之厚」者，羕言劉主分兒子厚恩，施之於己，故其書後語雲「負我慈父，罪有百死」也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Your subject Songzhi thinks “kindness of dividing sons” means Yang spoke of Lord Liu’s generous favour to sons as applied to himself; therefore his letter later says “I betrayed my kind father—crime deserving a hundred deaths.”〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi reads this as Peng Yang acknowledging Liu Bei’s fatherly favour—hence his later “I betrayed a kind father.”〉

sentences.zh: 羕一朝狂悖，自求葅醢，為不忠不義之鬼乎！

translations.literal: Yang in one morning went mad and perverse, seeking for himself minced pickle—becoming a ghost disloyal and unrighteous!
translations.idiomatic: In one rash hour I earned execution—must I die faithless?

sentences.zh: 先民有言，左手據天下之圖，右手刎咽喉，愚夫不為也。

translations.literal: The former people said: left hand grasping the Under Heaven’s maps, right hand cutting the throat—even a fool would not do it.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said no fool trades the realm for his throat.

sentences.zh: 況僕頗別菽麥者哉！

translations.literal: Moreover your servant can somewhat tell beans from wheat!
translations.idiomatic: I know beans from wheat—I am no fool.

sentences.zh: 所以有怨望意者，不自度量，苟以為首興事業，而有投江陽之論，不解主公之意，意卒感激，頗以被酒，侻失『老』語。

translations.literal: The reason there was resentful gaze was not measuring myself; rashly thinking I first raised the enterprise, yet there was talk of banishing to Jiangyang—not understanding the lord’s intent; intent finally moved by passion, somewhat because of wine, slip lost the “old” words.
translations.idiomatic: My resentment came from pride: I thought myself founder of your cause yet was sent to Jiangyang; wine loosened my tongue into the “old” insult.

sentences.zh: 此僕之下愚薄慮所致，主公實未老也。

translations.literal: This is what your servant’s lowest foolish shallow thought brought—the lord is truly not yet old.
translations.idiomatic: That was my petty panic—you are not old.

sentences.zh: 且夫立業，豈在老少，西伯九十，寧有衰志，負我慈父，罪有百死。

translations.literal: Moreover raising enterprise—how could it lie in old or young? Xibo at ninety—could he have declining intent? I betrayed my kind father—crime deserving a hundred deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Great deeds heed no age—King Wen was ninety; I wronged a father who treated me as a son—death a hundred times over is just.

sentences.zh: 至於內外之言，欲使孟起立功北州，戮力主公，共討曹操耳，寧敢有他志邪？

translations.literal: As for inner and outer words—I wished to make Mengqi raise merit in the northern province, join strength with the lord, together strike Cao Cao—how dare I have other intent?
translations.idiomatic: My talk with Ma Chao aimed only at northern service against Cao Cao—never treason.

sentences.zh: 孟起說之是也，但不分別其間，痛人心耳。

translations.literal: Mengqi’s reporting it was right—only he did not distinguish within—it pains the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao did right to report but blurred the context—it wounds me.

sentences.zh: 昔每與龐統共相誓約，庶託足下末踪，盡心於主公之業，追名古人，載勳竹帛。

translations.literal: Formerly I often with Pang Tong mutually swore covenant—hoped to entrust your footsteps’ tail end; exhaust heart in the lord’s enterprise; pursue fame with ancient men; load merit on bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Tong and I swore to serve your enterprise and win names on the histories.

sentences.zh: 統不幸而死，僕敗以取禍。

translations.literal: Tong unluckily died; your servant failed and drew calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He died; I stumbled into ruin.

sentences.zh: 自我墮之，將復誰怨！

translations.literal: I myself brought it down—whom again shall I resent!
translations.idiomatic: I alone am to blame.

sentences.zh: 足下，當世伊、呂也，宜善與主公計事，濟其大猷。

translations.literal: You, sir, are this age’s Yi Yin and Lü Wang—you ought well to plan affairs with the lord and aid his great strategy.
translations.idiomatic: You are this age’s Yi Yin—counsel the lord and finish his great design.

sentences.zh: 天明地察，神祇有靈，復何言哉！

translations.literal: Heaven bright and earth discerning—the spirits have insight—what more to say!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth know truth—what need of words!

sentences.zh: 貴使足下明僕本心耳。

translations.literal: I only value making you, sir, clear your servant’s original heart.
translations.idiomatic: I only beg you to know my heart.

sentences.zh: 行矣努力，自愛，自愛！

translations.literal: Go—strive hard; cherish yourself, cherish yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Farewell—take care, take care!

sentences.zh: 羕竟誅死，時年三十七。

translations.literal: Yang was executed in the end; at the time he was thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yang was executed at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 廖立

translations.literal: Liao Li
translations.idiomatic: Liao Li

sentences.zh: 〈廖音理救反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Liao is read li-jù fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The surname Liao is read with entering tone li-jù.〉

sentences.zh: 字公淵，武陵臨沅人。

translations.literal: Courtesy name Gongyuan; a man of Linyuan in Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Styled Gongyuan, from Linyuan in Wuling commandery.

sentences.zh: 先主領荊州牧，闢為從事，年未三十，擢為長沙太守。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord held governorship of Jing Province, he summoned him as attendant clerk; before age thirty he was promoted Governor of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei employed him in Jing and, before thirty, made him governor of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 先主入蜀，諸葛亮鎮荊土，孫權遣使通好於亮，因問士人皆誰相經緯者，亮答曰：「龐統、廖立，楚之良才，當贊興世業者也。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord entered Shu, Zhuge Liang guarded Jing’s territory; Sun Quan sent envoys to open goodwill with Liang and thereby asked which gentlemen managed warp and woof—Liang answered, saying, “Pang Tong and Liao Li are Chu’s fine talents—they should aid in raising the age’s enterprise.”
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Bei was in Shu, Zhuge Liang held Jing; Sun Quan’s envoy asked who shaped policy—Zhuge Liang named Pang Tong and Liao Li as Chu’s best men to build the realm.”

sentences.zh: 」建安二十年，權遣呂蒙奄襲南三郡，立脫身走，自歸先主。

translations.literal: ” In the twentieth year of Jian’an, Quan sent Lü Meng to suddenly raid the southern three commanderies; Li escaped and fled, returning himself to the Former Lord.
translations.idiomatic: In 215 Sun Quan seized the southern commanderies; Liao Li fled to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 先主素識待之，不深責也，以為巴郡太守。

translations.literal: The Former Lord had long known and treated him; did not blame deeply; made him Governor of Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei knew him well and blamed him lightly, naming him governor of Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，先主為漢中王，徵立為侍中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the Former Lord became King of Hanzhong and summoned Li as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 219, when Liu Bei became king of Hanzhong, Liao Li became palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 後主襲位，徙長水校尉。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord succeeded, he was transferred to Colonel of the Chang River Regiment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Shan he was shifted to colonel of the Chang River regiment.

sentences.zh: 立本意，自謂才名宜為諸葛亮之貳，而更遊散在李嚴等下，常懷怏怏。

translations.literal: Li’s original intent—he himself thought talent and name fitted him to be Zhuge Liang’s deputy; yet he wandered loosely below Li Yan and others; always harboured discontent.
translations.idiomatic: He believed himself Zhuge Liang’s natural deputy yet ranked below Li Yan—resentment festered.

sentences.zh: 後丞相掾〔李邵〕、蔣琬至，立計曰：

translations.literal: Later Chancellor’s aides [Li Shao], Jiang Wan arrived; Li plotted, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When clerks Li Shao and Jiang Wan came, Liao Li began his tirade:

sentences.zh: 軍當遠出，卿諸人好諦其事。

translations.literal: The army is about to go far out—you gentlemen should examine well its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: “The army marches far—mark what follows.”

sentences.zh: 昔先

translations.literal: Formerly the Former
translations.idiomatic: “Once your

translations.literal: (lord)
translations.idiomatic: 〈lord〉

sentences.zh: 不取漢中，走與吳人爭南三郡，卒以三郡與吳人，徒勞役吏士，無益而還。

translations.literal: did not take Hanzhong; ran to contend with Wu men for the southern three commanderies; in the end gave the three commanderies to Wu men—toiling clerks and soldiers for nothing and returning.
translations.idiomatic: former lord skipped Hanzhong to wrest the southern three counties from Wu—then handed them over for wasted sweat and nothing gained.”

sentences.zh: 既亡漢中，使夏侯淵、張郃深入於巴，幾喪一州。

translations.literal: Having lost Hanzhong, caused Xiahou Yuan and Zhang He to penetrate deep into Ba—almost lost one province.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong lost, Xiahou Yuan and Zhang He nearly carved up Ba commandery.”

sentences.zh: 後至漢中，使關侯身死無孑遺，上庸覆敗，徒失一方。

translations.literal: Later reaching Hanzhong, caused Lord Guan to die leaving no remnant; Shangyong overturned and defeated—empty loss of one region.
translations.idiomatic: Then Guan Yu died without heirs and Shangyong collapsed—another province wasted.”

sentences.zh: 是羽怙恃勇名，作軍無法，直以意突耳，故前後數喪師眾也。

translations.literal: This was Yu relying on his brave name, conducting armies without method—straightforwardly bursting by whim—therefore before and after repeatedly lost hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu trusted bravado, ignored discipline, charged by whim—again and again he wasted armies.”

sentences.zh: 如向朗、文恭，凡俗之人耳。

translations.literal: Such as Xiang Lang, Wen Gong—merely common vulgar men.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Lang and Wen Gong are mediocrity.”

sentences.zh: 恭作治中無綱紀；

translations.literal: Gong as administrative aide had no norm;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Gong ran the bureau without order;

sentences.zh: 朗昔奉馬良兄弟，謂為聖人，今作長史，素能合道。

translations.literal: Lang formerly served Ma Liang’s brothers, calling them sages; now as chief clerk—plainly able to match the Way?
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Lang once worshipped the Ma brothers as sages—now chief clerk and supposedly adequate?”

sentences.zh: 中郎郭演長，從人者耳，不足與經大事，而作侍中。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Household Guo Yanchang—a follower’s man only—not enough to manage great affairs, yet made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yanchang is a follower unfit for great matters—yet palace attendant.”

sentences.zh: 今弱世也，欲任此三人，為不然也。

translations.literal: Now is a weak age—wishing to entrust these three men—is not right.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusting the realm to such men in these times is folly.”

sentences.zh: 王連流俗，苟作掊克，使百姓疲弊，以致今日。

translations.literal: Wang Lian was vulgar fashion—rashly acted extortionist, causing the hundred surnames weary and ruined—bringing today.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lian taxed the people dry—here we sit.”

translations.literal: (He)
translations.idiomatic: 〈He〉

sentences.zh: 、琬具白其言於諸葛亮。

translations.literal: and Wan fully reported his words to Zhuge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shao and Jiang Wan reported every word to Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 亮表立曰：「長水校尉廖立，坐自貴大，臧否群士，公言國家不任賢達而任俗吏，又言萬人率者皆小子也；

translations.literal: Liang memorialized Li, saying: “Colonel of the Chang River Regiment Liao Li sits self-exalted; praises and blames the host of gentlemen; openly says the state does not employ worthy and enlightened men but employs vulgar clerks; also says commanders of ten thousand are all petty fellows;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang memorialised: “Liao Li glorifies himself, slanders everyone, claims we favour petty clerks over worthies, and calls our generals boys;

sentences.zh: 誹謗先帝，疵毀眾臣。

translations.literal: slanders the Former Lord; flaws and destroys the host of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: he insults the late emperor and smears his fellows.”

sentences.zh: 人有言國家兵眾簡練，部伍分明者，立舉頭視屋，憤吒作色曰：『何足言！

translations.literal: When someone spoke of the state’s troops numerous and drilled, ranks clear—Li raised his head, looked at the roof, angrily shouted and changed colour, saying: “What worth speaking!
translations.idiomatic: If anyone praised Shu’s disciplined hosts he rolled his eyes at the ceiling and snarled, “Rubbish!”

sentences.zh: 』凡如是者不可勝數。

translations.literal: ” Such as these cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Instances beyond count.”

sentences.zh: 羊之亂群，猶能為害，況立託在大位，中人以下識真偽邪？」

translations.literal: A goat disturbing the flock can still do harm—how much more Li entrusted in high place—can men below average tell true from false?”
translations.idiomatic: A stray goat upsets the herd—how much worse a fool near power—can common men judge him?”

sentences.zh: 〈亮集有亮表曰：「立奉先帝無忠孝之心，守長沙則開門就敵，領巴郡則有闇昧闟茸其事，隨大將軍則誹謗譏訶，侍梓宮則挾刃斷人頭於梓宮之側。

translations.literal: 〈In Liang’s collected works there is Liang’s memorial saying: “Li served the Former Lord without loyal filial heart; guarding Changsha then opened gates to the enemy; governing Ba Commandery then had dark stupid incompetence in affairs; following the Grand General then slandered and mocked; attending the catalpa palace then grasped blade and cut men’s heads beside the catalpa palace.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Zhuge Liang’s papers add: “Liao Li betrayed Changsha to the enemy, misruled Ba, mocked superiors, and drew steel beside the late emperor’s bier.”

sentences.zh: 陛下即位之後，普增職號，立隨比為將軍，面語臣曰：『我何宜在諸將軍中！

translations.literal: After Your Majesty ascended, offices broadly increased; Li followed comparison as general; face to face said to your servant: “How should I stand among the various generals!
translations.idiomatic: After your accession he took a general’s rank and told me: “How can I rank with mere generals!”

sentences.zh: 不表我為卿，上當在五校！

translations.literal: If you do not table me as minister, at minimum I should be among the Five Colonelcies!
translations.idiomatic: If not minister, I belong among the Five Colonelcies!”

sentences.zh: 』臣答：『將軍者，隨大比耳。

translations.literal: ” Your servant answered: “General means following the grand comparison.”
translations.idiomatic: I answered: “General matches your peers.”

sentences.zh: 至於卿者，正方亦未為卿也。

translations.literal: As for minister—even Zhengfang has not yet been minister.”
translations.idiomatic: Even Li Yan is not yet minister.”

sentences.zh: 且宜處五校。

translations.literal: For now you ought to stand among the Five Colonelcies.”
translations.idiomatic: Stay among the Five Colonelcies for now.”

sentences.zh: 』自是之後，怏怏懷恨。

translations.literal: ” From this afterward he was discontented and harboured resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He nursed a grudge ever after.”

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「三苗亂政，有虞流宥，廖立狂惑，朕不忍刑，亟徙不毛之地。」〉

translations.literal: ” An edict said: “Sanmiao disturbed government; Youyu banished with leniency—Liao Li is mad and deluded; We cannot bear punishment—hastily move him to barren land.”〉
translations.idiomatic: The edict compared him to the San Miao—banished, not executed, to the wilderness.〉

sentences.zh: 於是廢立為民，徙汶山郡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li was stripped to commoner and moved to Wenshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Li was reduced to commoner status and exiled to Wenshan.

sentences.zh: 立躬率妻子耕殖自守，聞諸葛亮卒，垂泣歎曰：「吾終為左衽矣！

translations.literal: Li personally led wife and children to farm and guard himself; hearing Zhuge Liang died, he wept and sighed, saying, “I shall end as left-lapelled!”
translations.idiomatic: He farmed with his family in exile; when Zhuge Liang died he wept, “I shall finish my days a barbarian!”

sentences.zh: 」後監軍姜維率偏軍經汶山、詣立，稱立意氣不衰，言論自若。

translations.literal: ” Later Army Supervisor Jiang Wei led a detached force passing Wenshan, visited Li—said Li’s spirit and intent did not decline; speech and discourse as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jiang Wei passed through and found him proud and articulate as ever.

sentences.zh: 立遂終徙所。

translations.literal: Li therefore ended at the place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: He died in exile.

sentences.zh: 妻子還蜀。

translations.literal: Wife and children returned to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His family returned to Shu.

sentences.zh: 李嚴字正方，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Yan, courtesy name Zhengfang, was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, styled Zhengfang, came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 少為郡職吏，以才幹稱。

translations.literal: In youth he was a county office clerk, famed for talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful clerical service brought him a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 荊州牧劉表使歷諸郡縣。

translations.literal: Governor of Jing Province Liu Biao had him serve successively through various commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao sent him through Jing’s counties and districts.

sentences.zh: 曹公入荊州時，嚴宰秭歸，遂西詣蜀，劉璋以為成都令，復有能名。

translations.literal: When Duke Cao entered Jing Province, Yan was magistrate of Zigui; then went west to Shu; Liu Zhang made him Prefect of Chengdu—again had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao took Jing, Li Yan governed Zigui, then crossed to Shu; Liu Zhang made him prefect of Chengdu—another mark of ability.

sentences.zh: 建安十八年，署嚴為護軍，拒先主於綿竹。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jian’an, Yan was appointed Protector of the Army, resisting the Former Lord at Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: In 213 Liu Zhang named him protector of the army to hold Liu Bei at Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 嚴率眾降先主，先主拜嚴裨將軍。

translations.literal: Yan led the host to surrender to the Former Lord; the Former Lord appointed Yan General of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan brought his command over to Liu Bei, who named him a general of the household.

sentences.zh: 成都既定，為犍為太守、興業將軍。

translations.literal: After Chengdu was settled, he became Governor of Qianwei and General Who Uplifts Enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengdu fell he governed Qianwei and held the title general who uplifts enterprise.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，盜賊馬秦、高勝等起事於郪，

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, bandits Ma Qin, Gao Sheng, and others rose in Qi,
translations.idiomatic: In 218 rebels Ma Qin and Gao Sheng rose at Qi,

sentences.zh: 〈音淒。〉

translations.literal: 〈Pronounced like qi (bleak).〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The place name is read like “bleak.”〉

sentences.zh: 合聚部伍數万人，到資中縣。

translations.literal: gathered bands numbering tens of thousands and reached Zizhong County.
translations.idiomatic: they gathered tens of thousands of followers and marched on Zizhong.

sentences.zh: 時先主在漢中，嚴不更發兵，但率將郡士五千人討之，斬秦、勝等首。

translations.literal: At the time the Former Lord was in Hanzhong; Yan did not further dispatch troops but led five thousand commandery gentlemen-soldiers to strike them; beheaded Qin, Sheng, and others’ heads.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei was in Hanzhong, so Li Yan raised no extra troops—only five thousand local troops—and took Ma Qin’s and Gao Sheng’s heads.

sentences.zh: 枝黨星散，悉复民籍。

translations.literal: Branch factions scattered like stars; all were restored to civilian registers.
translations.idiomatic: Their followers melted away and were returned to the tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 又越巂夷率高定遣軍圍新道縣，嚴馳往赴救，賊皆破走。

translations.literal: Moreover Yuexi Yi leader Gao Ding sent troops to surround Xindao County; Yan galloped to rescue; the bandits all broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Ding of Yuexi besieged Xindao, Li Yan rode to the rescue and routed them.

sentences.zh: 加輔漢將軍，領郡如故。

translations.literal: He was added General Who Assists Han, continuing to hold the commandery as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who assists Han while keeping Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 九年春，亮軍祁山，平催督運事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year, Liang’s army was at Qishan; Ping urged and supervised transport affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 231 Zhuge Liang was at Qishan; Li Ping oversaw supply runs.

sentences.zh: 秋夏之際，值天霖雨，運糧不繼，平遣參軍狐忠、督軍成籓喻指，呼亮來還；

translations.literal: Between autumn and summer it happened that Heaven sent continuous rain; grain transport did not continue; Ping sent staff adviser Hu Zhong and supervisor Cheng Fan with instructions, summoning Liang to return;
translations.idiomatic: Autumn rains cut the supply line; Li Ping sent Hu Zhong and Cheng Fan with orders for Zhuge Liang to pull back;

sentences.zh: 亮承以退軍。

translations.literal: Liang accepted and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang obeyed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 平聞軍退，乃更陽驚，說「軍糧饒足，何以便歸」！

translations.literal: When Ping heard the army had withdrawn, then feigned surprise, saying “Army grain is abundant—why return so soon!”
translations.idiomatic: Then Li Ping feigned shock: “We have plenty of grain—why retreat?”

sentences.zh: 欲以解己不辦之責，顯亮不進之愆也。

translations.literal: He wished thereby to excuse his own failure to deliver and display Liang’s fault for not advancing.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to blame Zhuge Liang for timidity and cover his own logistics failure.

sentences.zh: 又表後主，說「軍偽退，欲以誘賊與戰」。

translations.literal: He also memorialized the Later Lord, saying “The army feigned retreat, wishing thereby to lure the bandits to battle.”
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor the withdrawal was a ruse to lure Wei out.

sentences.zh: 亮具出其前後手筆書疏本末，平違錯章灼。

translations.literal: Liang produced in full his earlier and later handwritten letters and memorials’ beginning and end—Ping’s violation and error were manifestly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang produced their correspondence; Li Ping’s lies stood exposed.

sentences.zh: 平辭窮情竭，首謝罪負。

translations.literal: Ping’s words were exhausted and feeling spent; he bowed and confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Li Ping confessed.

sentences.zh: 於是亮表平曰：「自先帝崩後，平所在治家，尚為小惠，安身求名，無憂國之事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liang memorialized Ping, saying: “Since the Former Lord’s passing, wherever Ping has been he has managed his household, still doing petty kindnesses, securing himself and seeking fame—there are no affairs of worrying for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang wrote: “Since the late emperor died Li Ping has tended his private affairs, traded petty favours for reputation, and ignored the state.”

sentences.zh: 臣當北出，欲得平兵以鎮漢中，平窮難縱橫，無有來意，而求以五郡為巴州刺史。

translations.literal: When your servant should go north, I wished to obtain Ping’s troops to garrison Hanzhong; Ping raised difficulties in every direction and had no intent to come, yet sought to make five commanderies into Inspector of Ba Province.
translations.idiomatic: When I marched north I asked him to hold Hanzhong; he stalled and demanded to be inspector over five commanderies as Ba province.”

sentences.zh: 去年臣欲西征，欲令平主督漢中，平說司馬懿等開府闢召。

translations.literal: Last year your servant wished to campaign west and wished to order Ping to take charge of Hanzhong; Ping spoke of Sima Yi and others opening offices and summoning recruits.
translations.idiomatic: Last year I meant to leave him Hanzhong; he answered that Sima Yi was recruiting worthies.”

sentences.zh: 臣知平鄙情，欲因行之際偪臣取利也，是以表平子豐督主江州，隆崇其遇，以取一時之務。

translations.literal: Your servant knew Ping’s base intent—wishing on the march’s occasion to coerce your servant for profit; therefore your servant memorialized Ping’s son Feng to supervise Jiangzhou, greatly honouring his treatment, to settle the moment’s tasks.
translations.idiomatic: I knew he meant to profit from my absence, so I honoured his son Li Feng in Jiangzhou to keep him quiet.”

sentences.zh: 平至之日，都委諸事，群臣上下皆怪臣待平之厚也。

translations.literal: When Ping arrived, all affairs were entrusted to him; host of ministers above and below all marvelled at how thickly your servant treated Ping.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived I gave him full trust—the court marvelled at my generosity.”

sentences.zh: 正以大事未定，漢室傾危，伐平之短，莫若褒之。

translations.literal: Just because the great task was not settled and the Han house leaned toward peril—to attack Ping’s shortcomings was not as good as praising him.
translations.idiomatic: The realm still hung in the balance—praise worked better than blame.”

sentences.zh: 然謂平情在於榮利而已，不意平心顛倒乃爾。

translations.literal: Yet your servant thought Ping’s intent lay only in glory and profit—did not expect Ping’s heart to be upside-down thus.
translations.idiomatic: I thought he only cranked rank and wealth—I never dreamed he would sink this low.”

sentences.zh: 若事稽留，將致禍敗，是臣不敏，言多增咎。」

translations.literal: If affairs drag and delay, will bring calamity and defeat—this is your servant’s dullness; words add more fault.”
translations.idiomatic: If delay ruins the campaign, the fault is mine for trusting him too long.”

sentences.zh: 〈亮公文上尚書曰：「平為大臣，受恩過量，不思忠報，橫造無端，危恥不辦，迷罔上下，論獄棄科，導人為奸，

translations.literal: 〈Liang’s official document to the Ministry says: “Ping as great minister received favour beyond measure; did not think to repay with loyalty; recklessly created without cause; peril and shame unmet; deluded above and below; argued lawsuits abandoning statute; led men to wickedness,
translations.idiomatic: 〈Another memorial lists Li Ping’s crimes: ingratitude, invention, collapse of logistics, deceiving court and army—

sentences.zh: （狹情）

translations.literal: (narrow feeling)
translations.idiomatic: 〈variant: narrow sentiment〉

sentences.zh: 〔情狹〕志狂，若無天地。

translations.literal: [narrow of temper] ambition mad, as if without Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: petty, arrogant, as though heaven and earth did not exist.”

sentences.zh: 自度姦露，嫌心遂生，聞軍臨至，西鄉託疾還沮、漳，軍臨至沮，復還江陽，平參軍狐忠勤諫乃止。

translations.literal: Estimating himself exposed in treachery, suspicious heart then arose; hearing the army drew near, westward feigned illness returning to Ju and Zhang; when army drew near Ju, returned again to Jiangyang—Ping’s staff adviser Hu Zhong earnestly remonstrated and only then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sensing exposure he fled west toward Ju and Zhang, doubled back to Jiangyang, until his aide Hu Zhong stopped him.

sentences.zh: 今篡賊未滅，社稷多難，國事惟和，可以克捷，不可苞含，以危大業。

translations.literal: Now the usurping bandit is not yet destroyed; altars and grain face many hardships—state affairs rely on harmony to achieve victory; cannot wrap and contain to endanger the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Wei still stands; national crisis demands unity—we cannot shelter traitors and risk the realm.

sentences.zh: 輒與行中軍師車騎將軍都鄉侯臣劉琰，使持節前軍師征西大將軍領涼州刺史南鄭侯臣魏延、前將軍都亭侯臣袁綝、左將軍領荊州刺史高陽鄉侯臣吳壹、督前部右將軍玄鄉侯臣高翔、督後部後將軍安樂亭侯臣吳班、領長史綏軍將軍臣楊儀、督左部行中監軍揚武將軍臣鄧芝、行前監軍征南將軍臣劉巴、行中護軍偏將軍臣費禕、行前護軍偏將軍漢成亭侯臣許允、行左護軍篤信中郎將臣丁咸、行右護軍偏將軍臣劉敏、行護軍征南將軍當陽亭侯臣姜維、行中典軍討虜將軍臣上官雝、行中參軍昭武中郎將臣胡濟、行參軍建義將軍臣閻晏、行參軍偏將軍臣爨習、行參軍裨將軍臣杜義、行參軍武略中郎將臣杜祺、行參軍綏戎都尉盛勃、領從事中郎武略中郎將臣樊岐等議，輒解平任，免官祿、節傳、印綬、符策，削其爵土。」〉

translations.literal: Thereupon together with Acting Army Adviser General of Chariots and Cavalry Marquis of Dou Village Liu Yan, Bearer of Insignia Former Army Adviser Grand General Who Conquers the West Concurrent Inspector of Liang Province Marquis of Nan Zheng Wei Yan, Former General Marquis of Du Village Yuan Yi, Left General Concurrent Inspector of Jing Province Marquis of Gaoyang Village Wu Yi, Supervisor of Front Section General of the Right Marquis of Xuan Village Gao Xiang, Supervisor of Rear Section General of the Rear Marquis of Anle Village Wu Ban, Chief Clerk General Who Pacifies the Army Yang Yi, Supervisor of Left Section Acting Central Army Supervisor General Who Displays Might Deng Zhi, Acting Former Supervisor General Who Conquers the South Liu Ba, Acting Central Protector of the Army Lieutenant General Fei Yi, Acting Former Protector of the Army Lieutenant General Marquis of Hancheng Village Xu Yun, Acting Left Protector of the Army Faithful General of the Household Ding Xian, Acting Right Protector of the Army Lieutenant General Liu Min, Acting Protector of the Army General Who Conquers the South Marquis of Dangyang Village Jiang Wei, Acting Central Army Director General Who Punishes Barbarians Shangguan Yong, Acting Central Staff Adviser General of Brilliant Might Hu Ji, Acting Staff Adviser General Who Establishes Righteousness Yan Yan, Acting Staff Adviser Lieutenant General Cuan Xi, Acting Staff Adviser General of the Household Du Yi, Acting Staff Adviser General of Martial Stratagem Du Qi, Acting Staff Adviser Pacification Commandant of the Rong Sheng Bo, Concurrent Attendant Clerk General of Martial Stratagem Fan Qi, and others deliberated—thereupon removed Ping from office, stripped official salary, insignia courier, seals and ribbons, tallies and patents, and cut his noble lands.”〉
translations.idiomatic: After the named high commanders—Liu Yan, Wei Yan, Yuan Yi, Wu Yi, Gao Xiang, Wu Ban, Yang Yi, Deng Zhi, Liu Ba, Fei Yi, Xu Yun, Ding Xian, Liu Min, Jiang Wei, Shangguan Yong, Hu Ji, Yan Yan, Cuan Xi, Du Yi, Du Qi, Sheng Bo, Fan Qi, and the rest—jointly ruled, Li Ping was dismissed from every office, stripped of salary, courier baton, seals, tallies, and enfeoffment, and his noble lands were revoked.〉

sentences.zh: 乃廢平為民，徙梓潼郡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ping was reduced to commoner and moved to Zitong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping was reduced to commoner status and exiled to Zitong.

sentences.zh: 〈諸葛亮又與平子豐教曰：「吾與君父子戮力以獎漢室，此神明所聞，非但人知之也。

translations.literal: 〈Zhuge Liang again instructed Ping’s son Feng, saying: “I with you, father and son, joined strength to aid the Han house—this the spirits have heard, not only men know it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Zhuge Liang wrote Li Feng: “Your father and I laboured for Han—Heaven knows it.

sentences.zh: 表都護典漢中，委君於東關者，不與人議也。

translations.literal: Memorializing the Director of Retainers to govern Hanzhong, entrusting you at the eastern pass—not consulted with others.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to give him Hanzhong and you the eastern gate without debate.

sentences.zh: 謂至心感動，終始可保，何圖中乖乎！

translations.literal: I thought utmost hearts would move each other—beginning and end could be kept—who plotted mid-course betrayal!
translations.idiomatic: I trusted hearts would stay true—who foresaw this breach?

sentences.zh: 昔楚卿屢絀，亦乃克復，思道則福，應自然之數也。

translations.literal: Formerly Chu ministers were repeatedly dismissed—yet could recover; pondering the Way brings blessing—it answers nature’s reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers fall and rise again—virtue brings restoration.”

sentences.zh: 原寬慰都護，勤追前闕。

translations.literal: I beg you comfort the Director of Retainers and diligently pursue remedying former faults.
translations.idiomatic: Comfort your father and help him atone.”

sentences.zh: 今雖解任，形業失故，奴婢賓客百數十人，君以中郎參軍居府，方之氣類，猶為上家。

translations.literal: Now although office is removed, form and estate lose their old state—yet slaves, maids, and guests number over a hundred; you as Gentleman of the Household staff adviser dwell at headquarters—compared to peers of your kind, still count as upper households.
translations.idiomatic: Though dismissed he keeps scores of servants; you remain an attendant at headquarters—still a great house.”

sentences.zh: 若都護思負一意，君與公琰推心從事者，否可複通，逝可複還也。

translations.literal: If the Director of Retainers ponders fault with single mind, you and Gongyan push hearts and serve affairs—blocked can again open; departed can again return.
translations.idiomatic: If he owns his fault and you and Jiang Wan work in good faith, doors can reopen.”

sentences.zh: 詳思斯戒，明吾用心，臨書長嘆，涕泣而已。」〉

translations.literal: Think carefully on this warning; clarify my intent—facing the letter I sigh long; tears only.”〉
translations.idiomatic: Read this and know my heart—I sign in tears.”〉

sentences.zh: 十二年，平聞亮卒，發病死。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when Ping heard Liang died, he fell ill with grief and died.
translations.idiomatic: In 234 Li Ping died of grief when he heard Zhuge Liang was gone.

sentences.zh: 平常冀亮當自補复，策後人不能，故以激憤也。

translations.literal: Ping normally hoped Liang would himself restore him; gauging later men could not—therefore died of angry grief.
translations.idiomatic: He had counted on Zhuge Liang to reinstate him and despaired when no successor could.

sentences.zh: 〈習鑿齒曰：昔管仲奪伯氏駢邑三百，沒齒而無怨言，聖人以為難。

translations.literal: 〈Xi Zuochi says: Of old Guan Zhong seized the Bo clan’s three hundred households at Pian—until teeth fell none bore resentment—the sage thought this hard.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xi Zuochi recalls Guan Zhong’s confiscation—Bo’s clan never complained; Confucius called that rare.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮之使廖立垂泣，李平致死，豈徒無怨言而已哉！

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang’s making Liao Li weep and Li Ping die to the utmost—is it merely no resentful words!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang reduced Liao Li to tears and Li Ping to death—far beyond mere silence.”

sentences.zh: 夫水至平而邪者取法，鏡至明而醜者無怒，水鏡之所以能窮物而無怨者，以其無私也。

translations.literal: Water most level—crooked things take its rule; mirror most bright—ugly ones bear no anger—why water and mirror can exhaust things without resentment is because they are without private bias.
translations.idiomatic: Level water and bright mirrors judge without spite because they are impartial.

sentences.zh: 水鏡無私，猶以免謗，況大人君子懷樂生之心，流矜恕之德，法行於不可不用，刑加乎自犯之罪，爵之而非私，誅之而不怒，天下有不服者乎！

translations.literal: Water and mirror without private bias still thereby escape slander—how much more great men and gentlemen who harbour hearts rejoicing in life and pour forth forgiving virtue—law applied where it must be applied; punishment added to self-invited crime; ennobling without private motive; executing without anger—would Under Heaven have any who do not submit!
translations.idiomatic: When justice is dispensed without malice, who would not submit?

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮於是可謂能用刑矣，自秦、漢以來未之有也。〉

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang in this may be called able to use punishments—since Qin and Han there has not been his like.〉
translations.idiomatic: Never since Qin and Han had anyone wield punishment so fairly.〉

sentences.zh: 豐官至硃提太守。

translations.literal: Feng’s office reached Governor of Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Feng rose to governor of Zhu commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈蘇林《漢書音義》曰：硃音銖；

translations.literal: 〈Su Lin’s Sounds and Meanings for the Han Books says: Zhu is read like zhu (ounce);
translations.idiomatic: 〈Su Lin glosses Zhu like the weight zhu;

sentences.zh: 提音如北方人名匕曰提也。〉

translations.literal: ti is read like northerners calling the ladle bi as ti.〉
translations.idiomatic: ti as northerners say for “ladle.”〉

sentences.zh: 劉琰字威碩，魯國人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yan, courtesy name Weishuo, was a man of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, styled Weishuo, came from Lu.

sentences.zh: 先主在豫州，闢為從事，以其宗姓，有風流，善談論，厚親待之，遂隨從周旋，常為賓客。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord was in Yu Province, he summoned him as attendant clerk; because he shared the imperial surname, had polish, was skilled in discourse, treated him generously and intimately—thereupon followed in attendance, constantly as guest.
translations.idiomatic: In Yu province Liu Bei kept him as an attendant because he shared the imperial surname and cut a stylish figure—always a favoured companion.

sentences.zh: 先主定益州，以琰為固陵太守。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord pacified Yi Province, he made Yan Governor of Guling.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi fell Liu Yan governed Guling.

sentences.zh: 後主立，封都鄉侯，班位每亞李嚴，為衛尉中軍師後將軍，遷車騎將軍。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord ascended, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dou Village; court rank always second to Li Yan—was Minister of the Guards, Army Adviser of the Centre, General of the Rear; promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan made him village marquis of Dou, consistently ranked below Li Yan—minister of the guards, central army adviser, rear general, then general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 然不豫國政，但領兵千馀，隨丞相亮諷議而已。

translations.literal: Yet he did not participate in state governance—only commanded over a thousand troops, following Chancellor Liang in counsel and discussion only.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed out of policy with a thousand men on Zhuge Liang’s staff.

sentences.zh: 車服飲食，號為侈靡，侍婢數十，皆能為聲樂，又悉教誦讀魯靈光殿賦。

translations.literal: Carriages, robes, drink, and food were called extravagant; several tens of serving maids all could perform music and voice—also all taught to recite the Rhapsody on Lu’s Lingguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in notorious luxury with dozens of singing girls trained on the Lu Lingguang Hall rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 建興十年，與前軍師魏延不和，言語虛誕，亮責讓之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jianxing he did not get along with Former Army Adviser Wei Yan—speech hollow and wild; Liang rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: In 232 he quarrelled with Wei Yan with idle boasts until Zhuge Liang rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 琰與亮箋謝曰：「琰禀性空虛，本薄操行，加有酒荒之病，自先帝以來，紛紜之論，殆將傾覆。

translations.literal: Yan wrote a note to Liang apologizing, saying: “Yan’s received nature is hollow and empty; originally thin in conduct; moreover afflicted with wine’s wasteland disease—since the Former Lord, tangled talk has nearly overturned me.
translations.idiomatic: He apologised: “I am hollow by nature, loose in morals, and a drunkard—since the late emperor gossip nearly ruined me.”

sentences.zh: 頗蒙明公本其一心在國，原其身中穢垢，扶持全濟，致其祿位，以至今日。

translations.literal: Greatly received enlightened lord’s judging his single heart in the state, forgiving the filth within his person, supporting and completing him, bringing him to salary and rank—until today.
translations.idiomatic: You knew my heart was for Han and forgave my stains—raised me to rank.”

sentences.zh: 間者迷醉，言有違錯，慈恩含忍，不致之於理，使得全完，保育性命。

translations.literal: Recently deluded drunk—words had errors; kind grace bore and endured—not brought to judgment; allowed whole preservation, nurturing life.
translations.idiomatic: When wine led me astray you spared the law and saved my life.”

sentences.zh: 雖必克己責躬，改過投死，以誓神靈；

translations.literal: Although surely restraining self and blaming body, reforming faults and offering death—to swear to spirits;
translations.idiomatic: I would atone with my life,”

sentences.zh: 無所用命，則靡寄顏。

translations.literal: without place to use the mandate—then nowhere to rest face.
translations.idiomatic: yet if you dismiss me I have no face left.”

sentences.zh: 」於是亮遣琰還成都，官位如故。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Liang sent Yan back to Chengdu; office and rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang sent him back to Chengdu at full rank.

sentences.zh: 琰失志慌惚。

translations.literal: Yan lost intent and wandered confused.
translations.idiomatic: He drifted in confusion.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，琰妻胡氏入賀太后，太后令特留胡氏，經月乃出。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year’s first month, Yan’s wife Lady Hu entered to congratulate the Empress Dowager; the Empress Dowager ordered her specially detained—after a full month she emerged.
translations.idiomatic: In 234 his wife Lady Hu attended the empress dowager and was kept a month—rumours flew.

sentences.zh: 胡氏有美色，琰疑其與後主有私，呼

translations.literal: Lady Hu had beautiful looks; Yan suspected she had illicit ties with the Later Lord; summoned
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting an affair with the emperor, Liu Yan summoned

translations.literal: (soldiers)
translations.idiomatic: 〈text reads zu “soldiers”〉

sentences.zh: 五百撾胡，至於以履搏面，而後棄遣。

translations.literal: five hundred to flog Hu—even to striking her face with shoes—then cast her away.
translations.idiomatic: five hundred strokes and beat her face with shoes—then cast her out.

sentences.zh: 胡具以告言琰，琰坐下獄。

translations.literal: Hu reported everything in accusation of Yan; Yan sat and entered prison.
translations.idiomatic: She complained to the authorities and Liu Yan landed in jail.

sentences.zh: 有司議曰：「卒非撾妻之人，面非受履之地。

translations.literal: Authorities deliberated, saying: “Soldiers are not men who flog wives; face is not ground that receives shoes.
translations.idiomatic: The judges ruled: “Soldiers are not for beating wives; faces are not for shoes.”

sentences.zh: 」琰竟棄市。

translations.literal: ” Yan was executed in the end at the market.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 自是大臣妻母朝慶遂絕。

translations.literal: From this great ministers’ wives and mothers’ court congratulations ceased.
