translations.idiomatic: Court ladies’ New Year visits ended after that.

sentences.zh: 延每隨亮出，輒欲請兵萬人，與亮異道會於潼關，如韓信故事，亮製而不許。

translations.literal: Whenever Yan followed Liang out, he always wished to request ten thousand troops and meet Liang by a different route at Tong Pass, after Han Xin’s precedent—Liang restrained and did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan always wanted ten thousand men for a Han Xin–style strike on Tong Pass; Zhuge Liang refused.

sentences.zh: 延常謂亮為怯，嘆恨己才用之不盡。

translations.literal: Yan constantly called Liang timid; sighed and resented his own talent not fully used.
translations.idiomatic: He called Zhuge Liang timid and brooded over wasted talent.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：夏侯楙為安西將軍，鎮長安，亮於南鄭與群下計議，延曰：「聞夏侯楙少，主婿也，怯而無謀。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Summary says: Xiahou Mao was General Who Pacifies the West, garrisoned at Chang’an; Liang at Nan Zheng consulted subordinates; Yan said: “I hear Xiahou Mao is young—the lord’s son-in-law—timid and without stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei Summary records Wei Yan’s plan: Xiahou Mao holds Chang’an, young and cowardly—

sentences.zh: 今假延精兵五千，負糧五千，直從褒中出，循秦嶺而東，當子午而北，不過十日可到長安。

translations.literal: Now grant Yan elite troops five thousand, grain-bearing porters five thousand—straight out from Baozhong, follow Qinling eastward, strike Ziwu northward—within ten days can reach Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: give me ten thousand men through Baozhong along the Qin ridges—I could reach Chang’an in ten days.”

sentences.zh: 楙聞延奄至，必乘船逃走。

translations.literal: When Mao hears Yan arrives suddenly, he will surely flee by boat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Mao would flee by boat.

sentences.zh: 長安中惟有御史、京兆太守耳，橫門邸閣與散民之谷足週食也。

translations.literal: Within Chang’an there are only the Imperial Clerk and Jingzhao Governor; Heng Gate depot granaries and scattered commoners’ grain suffice for weeks of food.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial stores and public grain would feed us for weeks.

sentences.zh: 比東方相合聚，尚二十許日，而公從斜谷來，必足以達。

translations.literal: By the time the east joins and gathers, still about twenty-odd days—and you, sir, come from Xie Valley—surely sufficient to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty days before Wei mustered you could march from Xie Valley to join me.”

sentences.zh: 如此，則一舉而咸陽以西可定矣。

translations.literal: Like this, then with one stroke west of Xianyang can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Western Guanzhong would fall in one blow.”

sentences.zh: 」亮以為此縣危，不如安從坦道，可以平取隴右，十全必克而無虞，故不用延計。〉

translations.literal: ” Liang thought this path perilous—not as good as peacefully following the broad road, able calmly to take Longyou—tenfold whole sure to conquer without worry—therefore did not use Yan’s plan.〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang judged it too risky and preferred Longyou—so he passed on the scheme.〉

sentences.zh: 延既善養士卒，勇猛過人，又性矜高，當時皆避下之。

translations.literal: Yan was moreover good at nurturing soldiers—fierce bravery surpassing others—and nature proud and lofty; contemporaries all yielded below him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan inspired fierce loyalty and towering pride—everyone deferred.

sentences.zh: 唯楊儀不假借延，延以為至忿，有如水火。

translations.literal: Only Yang Yi showed Yan no indulgence; Yan took it as utmost resentment—like water and fire.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yang Yi stood up to him—they became fire and water.

sentences.zh: 十二年，亮出北谷口，延為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Liang went out North Valley mouth; Yan was vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In 234 Zhuge Liang took Ji Valley with Wei Yan in the van.

sentences.zh: 出亮營十里，延夢頭上生角，以問占夢趙直，直詐延曰：「夫麒麟有角而不用，此不戰而賊欲自破之像也。

translations.literal: Ten li out from Liang’s camp Yan dreamed horns grew on his head—asked dream-diviner Zhao Zhi; Zhi deceived Yan, saying: “The qilin has horns yet does not use them—this is an image of not battling yet the bandits wishing to break themselves.”
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan dreamed horns; Zhao Zhi lied that it meant victory without battle.”

sentences.zh: 」退而告人曰： 「角之為字，刀下用也；

translations.literal: ” Retreating he told others, saying: “The character for horn—knife beneath used;
translations.idiomatic: Privately Zhao Zhi said the word “horn” means knife upon head—

sentences.zh: 頭上用刀，其凶甚矣。」

translations.literal: knife upon the head—its ill-omen is extreme.”
translations.idiomatic: an ill omen atop the head.”

sentences.zh: 秋，亮病困，密與長史楊儀、司馬費禕、護軍姜維等作身歿之後退軍節度，令延斷後，姜維次之；

translations.literal: In autumn Liang fell gravely ill; secretly with Chief Clerk Yang Yi, Major Fei Yi, Protector of the Army Jiang Wei, etc., made arrangements for withdrawal after his death—ordered Yan to cover the rear, Jiang Wei next;
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Zhuge Liang, dying, secretly ordered Yang Yi, Fei Yi, and Jiang Wei to retreat with Wei Yan covering the rear and Jiang Wei next;

sentences.zh: 若延或不從命，軍便自發。

translations.literal: if Yan perhaps did not obey orders, the army would simply march on its own.
translations.idiomatic: if Wei Yan refused, march without him.

sentences.zh: 亮適卒，秘不發喪，儀令禕往揣延意指。

translations.literal: Liang had just died; mourning was kept secret; Yi ordered Yi to go gauge Yan’s intent.
translations.idiomatic: His death was concealed while Fei Yi sounded Wei Yan out.

sentences.zh: 延曰：「丞相雖亡，吾自見在。

translations.literal: Yan said: “Though the Chancellor has died, I myself still exist.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan said: “The chancellor is gone—I remain.”

sentences.zh: 府親官屬便可將喪還葬，吾自當率諸軍擊賊，云何以一人死廢天下之事邪？

translations.literal: Office kin and officials may escort the coffin home for burial—I ought myself to lead the various armies to strike the bandits—how can one man’s death abandon Under Heaven’s affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Send the body home—I will finish the campaign—how end the war for one death!”

sentences.zh: 且魏延何人，當為楊儀所部勒，作斷後將乎！

translations.literal: Moreover what manner of man is Wei Yan—to be commanded by Yang Yi and serve as rear guard general!
translations.idiomatic: And I, Wei Yan, take orders from Yang Yi as rear guard!”

sentences.zh: 」因與禕共作行留部分，令禕手書與己連名，告下諸將。

translations.literal: ” Therefore together with Yi he drafted marching and staying disposition; ordered Yi to hand-write joining his own name, proclaiming down to the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted orders with Fei Yi and asked him to cosign to the generals.

sentences.zh: 禕紿延曰：「當為君還解楊長史，長史文吏，稀更軍事，必不違命也。

translations.literal: Yi deceived Yan, saying: “I shall for you return and explain to Chief Clerk Yang—Chief Clerk is a civil clerk, seldom versed in military affairs—surely will not disobey orders.”
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi lied that he would persuade Yang Yi—the civil clerk would surely obey.”

sentences.zh: 」禕出門馳馬而去，延尋悔，追之已不及矣。

translations.literal: ” Yi went out the gate and galloped away; Yan soon regretted—pursuing him could not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi bolted; Wei Yan realised too late.

sentences.zh: 延遣人覘儀等，遂使欲案亮成規，諸營相次引軍還。

translations.literal: Yang sent men to spy on Yi and others; then ordered wishing to follow Liang’s standing rules—the various camps in succession led armies back.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan spied on Yang Yi’s camps withdrawing by Zhuge Liang’s plan.

sentences.zh: 延大怒，

translations.literal: Yan was greatly angry,
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan raged—

translations.literal: (before)
translations.idiomatic: 〈variant: cai “before”〉

sentences.zh: 儀未發，率所領徑先南歸，所過燒絕閣道。

translations.literal: before Yi had set out, led what he commanded straight south first—where he passed burned and cut gallery roads.
translations.idiomatic: before Yang Yi moved he raced south burning plank roads.

sentences.zh: 延、儀各相表叛逆，一日之中，羽檄交至。

translations.literal: Yan and Yi each mutual memorialized rebellion; within one day, feathered dispatches crossed in arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan and Yang Yi each denounced the other as a traitor; urgent dispatches crossed in a single day.

sentences.zh: 後主以問侍中董允、留府長史蔣琬，琬、允咸保儀疑延。

translations.literal: The Later Lord thereupon asked Palace Attendant Dong Yun and remaining headquarters Chief Clerk Jiang Wan; Wan and Yun all vouched for Yi and suspected Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan asked Dong Yun and Jiang Wan; both vouched for Yang Yi and distrusted Wei Yan.

sentences.zh: 儀等槎山通道，晝夜兼行，亦繼延後。

translations.literal: Yi and others cut mountain and opened road, day and night doubled march, also followed after Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi’s men cut through the mountains and marched night and day on Wei Yan’s heels.

sentences.zh: 延先至，據南谷口，遣兵逆擊儀等，儀等令何平在前禦延。

translations.literal: Yan arrived first, occupied South Valley mouth, sent troops to strike Yi and others head-on; Yi and others ordered He Ping in front to defend against Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan seized the southern valley and attacked; Yang Yi put He Ping in the van.

sentences.zh: 平叱延先登曰：「公亡，身尚未寒，汝輩何敢乃爾！

translations.literal: Ping scolded Yan for mounting first, saying: “The lord is dead; the body is not yet cold—how dare you act thus!
translations.idiomatic: He Ping rebuked him: “The chancellor is barely cold—how dare you do this!

sentences.zh: 」延士眾知曲在延，莫為用命，軍皆散。

translations.literal: ” Yan’s officers and masses knew the wrong lay with Yan; none obeyed orders—the army all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan’s men knew he was in the wrong and melted away.

sentences.zh: 延獨與其子數人逃亡，奔漢中。

translations.literal: Yan alone with his sons several fled, running to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He fled toward Hanzhong with a few followers.

sentences.zh: 儀遣馬岱追斬之，致首於儀，儀起自踏之，曰：「庸奴！

translations.literal: Yi sent Ma Dai to pursue and behead him; brought the head to Yi; Yi rose and trampled it himself, saying: “Worthless slave!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi sent Ma Dai, who sent back the head; Yang Yi trampled it, crying, “Villain!

sentences.zh: 復能作惡不？

translations.literal: Can you again do evil?”
translations.idiomatic: Can you still make trouble?

sentences.zh: 」遂夷延三族。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon exterminated Yan’s three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan’s kin to the third degree were executed.

sentences.zh: 初，蔣琬率宿衛諸營赴難北行，行數十里，延死問至，乃旋。

translations.literal: At first Jiang Wan led the inner guard’s various camps north on emergency—marched several dozen li; word of Yan’s death arrived—then turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan had marched north to intervene but turned back when word of Wei Yan’s death came.

sentences.zh: 原延意不北降魏而南還者，但欲除殺儀等。

translations.literal: The reason Yan's intent was not to surrender north to Wei but return south was only wishing to remove and kill Yi and others.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan did not mean to defect to Wei—he meant to kill Yang Yi.

sentences.zh: 平日諸將素不同，冀時論必當以代亮。

translations.literal: Yan with the various generals had never been in accord; he hoped public opinion would surely appoint him to replace Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He hoped rivals would name him Zhuge Liang’s heir.

sentences.zh: 本指如此。

translations.literal: His original intent was thus.
translations.idiomatic: That was his aim.

sentences.zh: 不便背叛。

translations.literal: Not convenient to betray.
translations.idiomatic: There was no plot to rebel.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：諸葛亮病，謂延等雲：「我之死後，但謹自守，慎勿複來也。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei Summary says: Zhuge Liang ill, said to Yan and others: “After my death, only guard yourselves strictly—carefully do not come again.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei Summary claims Zhuge Liang told Wei Yan: after his death hold fast—do not advance again.”

sentences.zh: 」令延攝行己事，密持喪去。

translations.literal: ” Ordered Yan to act in his affairs; secretly bore mourning away.
translations.idiomatic: He left secret funeral orders with Wei Yan.

sentences.zh: 延遂匿之，行至褒口，乃發喪。

translations.literal: Yan then concealed them; marched to Baokou—then proclaimed mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan concealed the death until Baokou.

sentences.zh: 亮長史楊儀宿與延不和，見延攝行軍事，懼為所害，乃張言延欲舉眾北附，遂率其眾攻延。

translations.literal: Liang’s Chief Clerk Yang Yi long had not been at peace with Yan; seeing Yan act in military affairs, feared being harmed by him—thereupon openly declared Yan wished to raise the host and attach north—thereupon led his host to attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi, fearing Wei Yan, accused him of defecting to Wei and attacked.

sentences.zh: 延本無此心，不戰軍走，追而殺之。

translations.literal: Yan originally lacked this intent—without battle the army fled—pursued and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan fled without fighting and was killed.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以為此蓋敵國傳聞之言，不得與本傳爭審。〉

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi thinks this is probably enemy-state hearsay talk—it cannot contend with the basic biography for examination.〉
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi treats this as hostile gossip, not the canonical story.〉

sentences.zh: 楊儀字威公，襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Yang Yi, courtesy name Weigong, was a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi, styled Weigong, came from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 建安中，為荊州刺史傅群主簿，背群而詣襄陽太守關羽。

translations.literal: In the Jian’an era he was Inspector of Jing Province Fu Qun’s chief clerk—turned against Qun and went to Xiangyang Governor Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He served Fu Qun of Jing then joined Guan Yu in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 羽命為功曹，遣奉使西詣先主。

translations.literal: Yu ordered him Merit Evaluator; sent him bearing mission west to the Former Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu made him merit evaluator and envoy to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 先主與語論軍國計策，政治得失，大悅之，因闢為左將軍兵曹掾。

translations.literal: The Former Lord with him discussed army and state plans, governance’s gains and losses—greatly pleased with him; therefore summoned him as Western Bureau Clerk of the Left General for Army Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei was so pleased with their talk of statecraft that he named him clerk of the Left General’s military bureau.

sentences.zh: 及先主為漢中王，拔儀為尚書。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord became King of Hanzhong, he promoted Yi to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei became king of Hanzhong, Yang Yi joined the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 先主稱尊號，東征吳，儀與尚書令劉巴不睦，左遷遙署弘農太守。

translations.literal: When the Former Lord assumed the exalted title and campaigned east against Wu, Yi and Director of the Ministry Liu Ba were not harmonious—demoted to distant concurrent Governor of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wu campaign he quarrelled with Liu Ba and was nominally posted to Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 建興三年，丞相亮以為參軍，署府事，將南行。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianxing Chancellor Liang made him staff adviser, acting headquarters affairs, about to go south.
translations.idiomatic: In 225 Zhuge Liang took him south as staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 五年，隨亮漢中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Liang to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In 227 he followed Zhuge Liang to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷長史，加綏軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted Chief Clerk and added General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 230 he became chief clerk and general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 亮數出軍，儀常規畫分部，籌度糧穀，不稽思慮，斯須便了。

translations.literal: Liang repeatedly led armies out; Yi constantly planned divisions, reckoned grain—not delaying thought—in a moment finished.
translations.idiomatic: He deployed columns and counted grain for every northern expedition with effortless speed.

sentences.zh: 軍戎節度，取辦於儀。

translations.literal: Military regulation—achievement lay with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign logistics ran through him.

sentences.zh: 亮深惜儀之才幹，憑魏延之驍勇，常恨二人之不平，不忍有所偏廢也。

translations.literal: Liang deeply prized Yi’s talent and capacity; relied on Wei Yan’s fierce bravery—constantly resented the two men’s lack of harmony—could not bear to favour one and discard the other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang prized Yang Yi’s staff work and Wei Yan’s valor yet could not reconcile them.

sentences.zh: 十二年，隨亮出屯谷口。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed Liang out to encamp at Valley mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In 234 he followed Zhuge Liang to Wuzhang Plain.

sentences.zh: 亮卒於敵場。

translations.literal: Liang died on the enemy field.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang died facing the enemy.

sentences.zh: 儀既領軍還，又誅討延，自以為功勳至大，宜當代亮秉政，呼都尉趙正以周易筮之，卦得家人，默然不悅。

translations.literal: Yi having led the army back and also punished and struck Yan, himself thought merit and deed extremely great—ought to replace Liang and hold governance—summoned Commandant Zhao Zheng to divine by the Zhou Changes—hexagram obtained Family—silent and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Wei Yan he expected to succeed Zhuge Liang—divining Family he fell silent.

sentences.zh: 而亮平生密指，以儀性狷狹，意在蔣琬，琬遂為尚書令、益州刺史。

translations.literal: Yet Liang’s lifelong secret intent—because Yi’s nature was harsh and narrow—intent lay in Jiang Wan—Wan then became Director of the Ministry and Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang had chosen Jiang Wan—who became director of the secretariat and governor of Yi.

sentences.zh: 儀至，拜為中軍師，無所統領，從容而已。

translations.literal: When Yi arrived, he was appointed Army Adviser of the Centre—nothing to command—ease only.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi received the hollow title central army adviser with no troops.

sentences.zh: 初，儀為先主尚書，琬為尚書郎，後雖俱為丞相參軍長史，儀每從行，當其勞劇，自惟年宦先琬，才能逾之，於是怨憤形於聲色，嘆吒之音發於五內。

translations.literal: At first Yi was the Former Lord’s Minister; Wan was Gentleman of the Palace; later although both were Chancellor staff chief clerks, Yi always followed on campaigns—bore the exhausting labour—himself thought seniority and office preceded Wan’s—talent surpassed him—thereupon resentment showed in voice and countenance; sighing tones issued from the five inner organs.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Yi’s senior and Jiang Wan’s junior, he now nursed grievance that Jiang Wan had leapfrogged him.

sentences.zh: 時人畏其言語不節，莫敢從也，惟後軍師費禕往慰省之。

translations.literal: People of the time feared his speech lacked restraint—none dared follow—only Rear Army Adviser Fei Yi went to console him.
translations.idiomatic: Men shunned his rants—only Fei Yi comforted him.

sentences.zh: 儀對禕恨望，前後云云，又語禕曰：「往者丞相亡沒之際，吾若舉軍以就魏氏，處世寧當落度如此邪！

translations.literal: Yi toward Yi harboured resentment and gaze—before and after thus and so—also said to Yi: “Formerly when the Chancellor died—if I had raised the army to join Wei—living in the age would I fall this low!
translations.idiomatic: He told Fei Yi that he could have defected to Wei when Zhuge Liang died—

sentences.zh: 令人追悔不可複及。

translations.literal: making men regret unable to reach again.”
translations.idiomatic: —and now could only regret it.

sentences.zh: 」禕密表其言。

translations.literal: ” Yi secretly memorialized his words.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi reported his words.

sentences.zh: 十三年，廢儀為民，徙漢嘉郡。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Yi was stripped to commoner and moved to Hanjia Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 235 he was reduced to commoner and exiled to Hanjia.

sentences.zh: 儀至徙所，复上書誹謗，辭指激切，遂下郡收儀。

translations.literal: When Yi reached the place of exile, again memorialized slander—word and thrust fierce and cutting—thereupon ordered commandery seize Yi.
translations.idiomatic: From exile he sent abusive memorials and was arrested.

sentences.zh: 儀自殺，其妻子還蜀。

translations.literal: Yi killed himself; his wife and children returned to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He committed suicide; his family returned to Shu.

sentences.zh: 〈楚國先賢傳云：儀兄慮，字威方。

translations.literal: 〈The Chu Worthies Traditions states: Yi’s elder brother Lü, courtesy name Weifang.
translations.idiomatic: 〈His elder brother Yang Lü, styled Weifang:

sentences.zh: 少有德行，為江南冠冕。

translations.literal: In youth had virtue and conduct—was Jiangnan’s crown.
translations.idiomatic: the moral paragon of the south.

sentences.zh: 州郡禮召，諸公闢請，皆不能屈。

translations.literal: Province and commandery ritual summoned; various lords summoned and requested—all could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every honour the region offered.

sentences.zh: 年十七，夭，鄉人號曰德行楊君。〉

translations.literal: At age seventeen, died young; village people styled him Worthy Yang of Virtue.〉
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventeen and was remembered as “the virtuous Lord Yang.”〉

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: 【Appraisal】

sentences.zh: 評曰：劉封處嫌疑之地，而思防不足以自衛。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Liu Feng stood in a place of suspicion and doubt—yet thought and guard were insufficient to protect himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Feng lived under suspicion without the caution to survive.

sentences.zh: 彭羕、廖立以才拔進，李嚴以幹局達，魏延以勇略任，楊儀以當官顯，劉琰舊仕，並咸貴重。

translations.literal: Peng Yang and Liao Li advanced by talent’s elevation; Li Yan rose by administrative grasp; Wei Yan was entrusted by fierce strategy; Yang Yi showed forth by holding office; Liu Yan was long in service—all alike honoured and weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yang, Liao Li, Li Yan, Wei Yan, Yang Yi, and Liu Yan each rose on talent, grit, or old service.

sentences.zh: 覽其舉措，跡其規矩，招禍取咎，無不自己也。

translations.literal: View their acts and measures; trace their norms and rules—summoning calamity and drawing blame—none was not from themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Their falls came from their own choices.
